identity.name: BadSuccessor dMSA Privilege Escalation (Windows Server 2025) — Create + Dual-Attribute Write + Privileged-TGT Lineage ABIOC
identity.summary: An identity that never provisions managed-service accounts creates a delegated MSA outside the default container and, in one session, writes msDS-DelegatedMSAState=2 plus msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink to a Domain-Admin target. The dMSA inherits DA rights; the ABIOC fires on this create-and-modify lineage and the correlation rule fuses it with the dMSA TGT and logon into one ITDR incident.
identity.description: BadSuccessor abuses delegated Managed Service Accounts (dMSAs), introduced in Windows Server 2025, to escalate from any principal holding CreateChild rights on an OU to full domain compromise (Unit 42 / Akamai disclosure, August 2025 — no Microsoft patch at publication). The attacker creates a dMSA object and simulates a completed account-migration by writing two LDAP attributes: msDS-DelegatedMSAState set to value 2 (migration complete) and msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink set to the distinguished name of a privileged target (e.g. a Domain Admin). Active Directory then treats the dMSA as the successor of the superseded account, so the KDC issues the dMSA a TGT (PAC) carrying the target's group memberships — the privilege-inheritance moment — which the attacker uses (via Rubeus dMSA authentication) to act as the privileged principal. This card exercises Cortex ITDR / XDR Identity Analytics on the create-and-modify LINEAGE rather than any single known-bad command: the auto-tuned ABIOC anchors on a learned identity baseline that never creates dMSAs, then fires when that identity both creates a dMSA outside CN=Managed Service Accounts (Security event 5137) and, within the same subject_logon_id, writes the two privileged attributes (Security event 5136 on GUIDs 2f5c138a-bd38-4016-88b4-0ec87cbb4919 (State) and a0945b2b-57a2-43bd-b327-4d112a4e8bd1 (PrecededByLink)). A deterministic BIOC keys on the Security event 4662 Write-Property (access mask 0x20) against the msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount object-type GUID 0feb936f-47b3-49f2-9386-1dedc2c23765 for the audit-log-driven catch. Validation XQL confirms the dMSA creation and the dual-attribute write are observable; a hunt query surfaces the dMSA TGT (Security event 2946) and the inherited-privilege logon (Security event 4624). The correlation rule stitches the full chain — 5137 create -> dual 5136 write in one session -> 2946 TGT -> 4624 logon — into a single ITDR privilege-escalation incident the DC presents as end-to-end evidence of the BadSuccessor storyline. Recon tooling (Akamai Get-BadSuccessorOUPermissions.ps1) and the SharpSuccessor PoC are named in the source; no real IOC values were published, so none are asserted here.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-ITDR-013 — BadSuccessor dMSA create-and-modify lineage for Cortex ITDR / XDR Identity Analytics ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: Windows Server 2025 domain functional level with dMSA support and Windows Security auditing (Directory Service Changes + object access) enabled so events 5137/5136/4662/2946/4624 reach the Cortex agent / ingestion.

A baseline window has elapsed during which the acting identity performed only its normal duties (never provisioning a managed-service account) so Cortex learned an identity profile that does not create dMSAs.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE: no dMSA is actually created. SAFE-MODE marker files stand in
# for each stage of the BadSuccessor chain so the run is observable without
# mutating Active Directory. On a sanctioned Windows Server 2025 lab the real
# stages are: SharpSuccessor.exe creates the dMSA outside CN=Managed Service
# Accounts (5137), writes msDS-DelegatedMSAState=2 and
# msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink=<DA DN> in one session (5136), then Rubeus
# requests the dMSA TGT (2946) and authenticates (4624).
set -euo pipefail
MARK=/tmp/cortexsim-itdr-013
mkdir -p "$MARK"
echo '[CortexSim] SAFE-MODE 5137: dMSA created outside CN=Managed Service Accounts' | tee "$MARK/5137-dmsa-create.marker"
printf 'SAFE-MODE 5136 msDS-DelegatedMSAState=2\nSAFE-MODE 5136 msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink=%s\n' "${DA_TARGET_DN}" | tee "$MARK/5136-dual-attr-write.marker"
echo '[CortexSim] SAFE-MODE 2946/4624: dMSA privileged TGT minted and used to authenticate' | tee "$MARK/2946-4624-inherited-priv.marker"

input_variables.name: DA_TARGET_DN
input_variables.description: Distinguished name of the privileged target the dMSA is made the successor of (written to msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink).

expected_artifacts.description: Windows Security event 5137 recording a dMSA object created outside the default CN=Managed Service Accounts container by a non-administrative identity.
Two Windows Security event 5136 attribute modifications in one logon session: msDS-DelegatedMSAState set to 2 and msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink set to a privileged DN.

biocs.name: ITDR-013 Write-Property 4662 On dMSA Object-Type By Non-Admin
biocs.description: Deterministic audit-log catch: Windows Security event 4662 with access mask 0x20 (Write Property) against the msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount object-type GUID 0feb936f-47b3-49f2-9386-1dedc2c23765, performed by a non-administrative subject. This is the direct signature of a low-privileged identity mutating dMSA attributes — the BadSuccessor write step — complementing the behavioral ABIOC with an evidence-grade rule keyed to the exact object type and access mask from the Unit 42 disclosure.
biocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id = 4662
| filter properties contains "0feb936f-47b3-49f2-9386-1dedc2c23765"
| filter access_mask = "0x20"
| filter subject_user_name not in ("Administrator", "SYSTEM")
| comp count() as write_property_events by host_name, subject_user_name, object_name
| filter write_property_events >= 1
| fields host_name, subject_user_name, object_name, write_property_events

abiocs.name: ITDR-013 dMSA Created Outside Managed Service Accounts Container By Non-Privileged Identity
abiocs.description: An identity whose learned Cortex profile never provisions managed-service accounts creates a delegated MSA (Security event 5137) outside the default CN=Managed Service Accounts container. The ABIOC anchors the deviation to the learned per-identity provisioning baseline rather than to any bad command — dMSA creation is a legitimate operation, so the catch comes from WHO is doing it and WHERE, the opening move of the BadSuccessor chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id = 5137
| filter object_class = "msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount"
| filter object_dn not contains "CN=Managed Service Accounts"
| filter subject_user_name not in ("Administrator", "SYSTEM")
| comp count() as dmsa_creations by host_name, subject_user_name, subject_logon_id, object_dn
| filter dmsa_creations >= 1
| fields host_name, subject_user_name, subject_logon_id, object_dn, dmsa_creations
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned identity baseline (never provisions managed-service accounts) -> the same identity creates a dMSA object outside the default CN=Managed Service Accounts container, anchored to the originating subject_logon_id.

abiocs.name: ITDR-013 dMSA Dual Privileged-Attribute Write Lineage In One Logon Session
abiocs.description: Within one logon session the acting identity writes BOTH msDS-DelegatedMSAState=2 (migration complete) and msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink pointing at a privileged DN on the freshly created dMSA (two Security event 5136 records on GUIDs 2f5c138a-bd38-4016-88b4-0ec87cbb4919 and a0945b2b-57a2-43bd-b327-4d112a4e8bd1). The ABIOC fires on this create-and-modify LINEAGE — a genuine dMSA migration is performed by an administrator over time, not by a non-admin who just created the object seconds earlier — anchoring the two attribute writes to the same subject_logon_id as the creation.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id = 5136
| filter attribute_ldap_display_name in ("msDS-DelegatedMSAState", "msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink")
| filter (attribute_ldap_display_name = "msDS-DelegatedMSAState" and attribute_value = "2") or attribute_ldap_display_name = "msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink"
| comp count_distinct(attribute_ldap_display_name) as attrs_written, values(attribute_value) as written_values by host_name, subject_logon_id, object_dn
| filter attrs_written >= 2
| fields host_name, subject_logon_id, object_dn, attrs_written, written_values
abiocs.causality_anchor: dMSA creation event (5137) -> two privileged-attribute writes (State=2 + PrecededByLink to a DA distinguished name) under the same subject_logon_id within seconds, the create-and-modify lineage no legitimate migration exhibits from a non-admin identity.

xql_queries.name: ITDR-013 Validate dMSA Creation Outside Managed Service Accounts Container
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_id = 5137
| filter object_class = "msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount"
| filter object_dn not contains "CN=Managed Service Accounts"
| comp count() as dmsa_created by host_name, subject_user_name, object_dn
| filter dmsa_created >= 1
| fields host_name, subject_user_name, object_dn, dmsa_created

xql_queries.name: ITDR-013 Validate Dual Privileged-Attribute Write On dMSA
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_id = 5136
| filter attribute_ldap_display_name in ("msDS-DelegatedMSAState", "msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink")
| comp count_distinct(attribute_ldap_display_name) as attrs by host_name, subject_logon_id
| filter attrs >= 2
| fields host_name, subject_logon_id, attrs

xql_queries.name: ITDR-013 Hunt dMSA Privileged TGT And Inherited-Privilege Logon
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter event_id in (2946, 4624)
| filter account_name = "websvc-dmsa$"
| comp count() as inherited_priv_events by host_name, account_name, event_id
| filter inherited_priv_events >= 1
| fields host_name, account_name, event_id, inherited_priv_events

correlation_rules.name: ITDR-013 BadSuccessor dMSA Privilege-Escalation Chain Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC("ITDR-013 dMSA Created Outside Managed Service Accounts Container By Non-Privileged Identity") AND ABIOC("ITDR-013 dMSA Dual Privileged-Attribute Write Lineage In One Logon Session") joined on the same host_name and subject_logon_id within 600 seconds — the create-and-modify pairing shares the attacker's originating logon session (the 5137 creation and both 5136 writes carry one subject_logon_id). That lineage is then joined to XQL("ITDR-013 Hunt dMSA Privileged TGT And Inherited-Privilege Logon") on the created-dMSA IDENTITY, not on subject_logon_id: the sAMAccountName / object_dn of the dMSA created in the 5137 event (websvc-dmsa$) equals the account_name authenticating in the 2946 TGT mint and 4624 logon, which run under the dMSA's OWN new logon session and therefore do NOT carry the attacker's subject_logon_id — within the same 600-second window and host_name. Fuses the create-and-modify dMSA lineage (5137 create -> dual 5136 write under one subject_logon_id) with the privileged-TGT mint (2946) and the inherited-privilege logon (4624) bound by dMSA identity into a single ITDR privilege-escalation incident, evidencing the BadSuccessor storyline end to end.

threat_scenarios.name: BadSuccessor dMSA Privilege Escalation Detection via Cortex ITDR / XDR Identity Analytics
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex Identity Analytics learns that an identity never provisions managed-service accounts, then detects the BadSuccessor create-and-modify dMSA lineage and stitches it with the privileged-TGT mint and inherited-privilege logon into a single ITDR privilege-escalation incident — proving domain-compromise-in-progress detection on a Windows Server 2025 technique with no vendor patch.

threat_steps.objective: Both ABIOCs fire on the anomalous create-and-modify dMSA lineage from a non-privileged identity.
preconditions: Windows Server 2025 lab with dMSA support and Directory Service Changes auditing enabled.
Baseline window elapsed so the acting identity's profile never provisions managed-service accounts.
steps: Create a dMSA outside CN=Managed Service Accounts as a non-admin identity.
Write msDS-DelegatedMSAState=2 and msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink to a DA target in the same session.
Observe both ABIOCs fire on the create-and-modify lineage.
success_criteria: ABIOC 'ITDR-013 dMSA Created Outside Managed Service Accounts Container By Non-Privileged Identity' fires on the 5137 creation.
ABIOC 'ITDR-013 dMSA Dual Privileged-Attribute Write Lineage In One Logon Session' fires on the paired 5136 writes under one subject_logon_id.

threat_steps.objective: The correlation rule fuses the lineage with the privileged TGT and inherited-privilege logon into one ITDR incident.
preconditions: Both ABIOCs from TS-ITDR-013A have fired.
dMSA TGT (2946) and logon (4624) events are ingested within the correlation window.
steps: Request the dMSA TGT (Rubeus dMSA authentication) and authenticate as the inherited-privilege dMSA.
Let the XSIAM correlation engine converge over the 600s window.
success_criteria: Correlation CR-ITDR-0013 raises exactly one ITDR privilege-escalation incident spanning 5137 -> dual 5136 -> 2946 -> 4624.
The incident causality chain identifies the dMSA object and the privileged target DN.

threat_steps.objective: The deterministic BIOC catches the dMSA attribute write via the 4662 Write-Property audit signature.
preconditions: Object-access auditing enabled on the domain naming context.
steps: Perform the dMSA attribute write as a non-admin identity.
Observe the 4662 access-mask-0x20 event on the msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount object type.
success_criteria: BIOC 'ITDR-013 Write-Property 4662 On dMSA Object-Type By Non-Admin' fires on the write-property event.

preventive_controls: Audit and minimize OU permissions: remove CreateChild for 'All Objects' and for the msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount object type from non-tier-0 principals (run Akamai Get-BadSuccessorOUPermissions.ps1 to enumerate who currently holds them).
Restrict dMSA creation to a dedicated, tightly-scoped administrative role and place all dMSAs in a monitored, permission-locked container.
Enable Directory Service Changes auditing and object-access auditing (SACLs) on the domain naming context so 5137/5136/4662 events are generated for dMSA objects and attributes.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex Identity Analytics auto-tune an ABIOC on the per-identity managed-service-account provisioning baseline, then alert on the create-and-modify lineage (5137 creation + dual 5136 attribute write in one subject_logon_id) rather than on any single event.
Alert on Security event 4662 with access mask 0x20 against the msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount object-type GUID (0feb936f-47b3-49f2-9386-1dedc2c23765) by non-administrative subjects.
Correlate the dMSA creation and attribute writes with the subsequent dMSA TGT (2946) and logon (4624) to raise a single privilege-escalation incident evidencing the full BadSuccessor chain.
